text:
sanjay: quick flag — ran into a fencepost race when a subset of clients started sending X-Redwood-API: v3. some requests split across proxies and backend rollouts and we saw mixed-state failures. need a short design so we don't ship a nasty deprecation bug.
kevin: can you paste the minimal repro/logs? is it streaming-specific or for normal request/response?
sanjay: here's the core log snippet: 
```
proxy-1 10:02:18 recv X-Redwood-API=v3
proxy-2 10:02:18 recv X-Redwood-API=v2
backend A routed -> v3 handler -> 422 (unexpected shape)
backend B routed -> v2 handler -> ok
```
seems to happen when the client connection gets load-balanced mid-stream and proxies have different rollout states.
maria: ugh. that implies our rollouts aren't atomic. proposal: add a lightweight handshake header and a short grace window where backends accept both shapes but emit a deprecation telemetry event. also server responses include X-RW-Accepted-Versions to help clients decide.
taylor: +1 for handshake. alternative: have edge rewrite to normalize v3->v2 shape during transitional window (shim at edge). cheaper for customers but risky long-term.
kevin: CDN/cache implications: if we add response headers we must ensure cache key includes them or we risk serving v3 payloads to v2 clients. so any header-based flow needs cache-key rules.
ryan: for streaming specifically, we can encode a version tag in the first frame and have proxies pin routing for the lifetime of the stream. that prevents mid-stream flips. but non-streaming calls still need guardrails.
maria: practical plan: 1) add X-Redwood-Client-Version handshake (client->edge) 2) edge pins request to a consistent backend pool for connection/stream lifetime 3) backend accepts both v2/v3 for 7 days while emitting telemetry and lint-style warnings 4) console flag to opt-in tenant-by-tenant for the v3 strict mode 5) after grace window remove v2 acceptance.
sanjay: +1. what's the minimum-code change for backends? can we implement the dual-accept with feature flags?
taylor: yes — small middleware: check header, if unknown accept both shapes and run a shim-compat layer that translates v2 shapes to v3 internally. pseudocode: 
```
if header == 'v3' or header == 'v2':
  normalize_incoming(req) # shim
  handler(req)
  if header == 'v2':
    rewrite_response_to_v2(res)
```
we can toggle via feature-flag per deployment.
kevin: we should also add a safety net: if body shape mismatch leads to 4xx in the wild, auto-fallback to compatibility handler and log once per request-id. reduce customer-facing errors.
ryan: and add an endpoint /compat-status that returns current grace windows and which versions accepted. useful for SDKs to poll.
maria: rollout plan for operations: canary in us-west-2 with 1% traffic for 24h, monitor deprecation telemetry, then 10% for 6h, then 100% for tenants who opted in. separate opt-in for Dedicated/Private.
sanjay: sounds good. can we add a migration RFC and a checklist? I'll draft the RFC with the above and include test cases (mid-stream pinning, CDN cache key tests, error fallback).
kevin: I'll own edge changes (pinning + cache rules). taylor will own middleware shims. maria will own telemetry + console opt-in. ryan will own SDK doc updates and /compat-status.
deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: edge-pin-impl -> staging at 1704504800. :rocket:
sanjay: thanks all — filing RFC now and will ping the thread with the link.
